purpose: Unlock Protocol governance turnout over the last ~600k Base blocks (~14 days, block ~53,084,185) — the decisive evidence that the cheap-quorum capture is deterred.
method: eth_getLogs on UPGovernor 0x65bA0624403Fc5Ca2b20479e9F626eD4D78E0aD9 for ProposalCreated (topic0 0x7d84a626…) and VoteCast (topic0 0xb8e13888…), decoded weight from the non-indexed data.

live_delegate_votes_now.0x38b826a4426a0d4d9b4377ac57c9af0308281c: 3420168687558954149098283 (EOA, code size 3) — MORE than the 3,000,000 quorum

implication: Observed turnout is 6.58M AGAINST to 13.85M FOR — i.e. 2.2x to 4.6x the 3,000,000 quorum.
A SINGLE delegate (0x38b826a4…) already holds 3.42M UP of voting power (> quorum, > the attacker's 3M) and demonstrably votes AGAINST proposals it dislikes (prop 11790216226306).
Buying 3M UP from the pool does NOT reduce these delegates' holdings, so the attacker's 3M would be outvoted by one attentive delegate.

To be safe the attacker would need >13.85M UP; buying 13.85M from the UP/WETH 0.3% pool (18.31M UP / 6.156 WETH) costs ~18.9 WETH = ~$44.5k with a ~$35k non-recoverable price impact (the stake must be held 4 days through the snapshot, so it cannot be flash-loaned or round-tripped) — net-negative versus the ~$29k realizable prize.

=> the cheap-quorum capture is deterred; E-U ~ $0. The residual is a governance-behaviour risk (if all active delegates abstain for the 6-day window) plus a liquidity risk (deeper UP pools would make >13.9M cheap to acquire).
